questions.question: How should students board a school bus?

options.text: In a single-file line.
Two at a time.
In as large a group as possible.
However they want to.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a single-file line.
questions.explanation: Students should board slowly in a single-file line while holding the handrails.

questions.question: When checking air and electrical lines, which statement is NOT true?

options.text: The air hoses are making a hissing noise.
The air hoses and electrical lines are not cut.
The air lines are not pinched.
The air lines are not dragging against tractor parts.

questions.correctAnswerText: The air hoses are making a hissing noise.
questions.explanation: Listen for leaks when checking air and electrical lines. The lines should not be cut, worn, tangled, pinched, or dragging. A hissing noise means there is a leak.

questions.question: What should you NOT do when checking the steering box?

options.text: Ensure that the steering box is securely mounted.
Ensure that the steering box is free of leaks.
Look for missing bolts in the steering box.
Assume all cotter keys are present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume all cotter keys are present.
questions.explanation: Check that the steering box is securely mounted. Look for missing nuts, bolts, and cotter keys. Make sure there are no power steering fluid leaks and no damaged hoses.

questions.question: If you must stop before turning during the skills test, what should you do?

options.text: Skid to a stop.
Stop after the stop line to see better.
Allow your vehicle to roll.
Keep the front wheels aimed straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the front wheels aimed straight ahead.
questions.explanation: Come to a smooth stop behind the stop line, crosswalk, or stop sign. Keep your front wheels straight and do not let the vehicle roll. Stop where you can still see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.question: What is true about loading a school bus?

options.text: It is not a dangerous process.
It does not need supervision.
It should be done quickly.
It can be dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: More students are killed during loading and unloading than while riding. Bus drivers must follow safety procedures during these times.

questions.question: Why should a school bus stop a short distance from waiting students?

options.text: Students will walk to the bus, so the driver can watch them better.
Students will usually be waiting on a sidewalk.
Students may get scared if the bus comes too close.
Buses are difficult to drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Students will walk to the bus, so the driver can watch them better.
questions.explanation: Stop at least 10 feet away from waiting students. This makes them walk to the bus, allowing the driver to see their movements clearly.

questions.question: What must you do when checking engine belts during inspection?

options.text: Check belts for snugness, allowing up to three inches of play.
The water pump belt does not need to be identified.
Remove the air compressor belt.
Identify any items that are not belt-driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: Identify any items that are not belt-driven.
questions.explanation: Check the power steering, water pump, alternator, and air compressor belts for cracks and frays. Allow up to three-quarters of an inch of play at the center of each belt. If any items are not belt-driven, identify them and check that they work properly, are not damaged or leaking, and are mounted securely.

questions.question: If a school bus must be evacuated, passengers should:

options.text: Always use the rear door.
Always use the windows.
Always use the front door.
Use the safest exit available.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the safest exit available.
questions.explanation: In an emergency, the driver must quickly decide which exit is safest and direct students to use it.

questions.question: What is true about pull-ups during the basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: Points are deducted for each pull-up.
A driver is allowed three pull-ups per maneuver.
A pull-up will earn points only if the driver gets out of the vehicle.
Only an excessive number of pull-ups counts as errors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only an excessive number of pull-ups counts as errors.
questions.explanation: One pull-up does not result in penalties. However, too many pull-ups will count as errors.

questions.question: When driving a school bus near railroad tracks, your four-way flashers should:

options.text: Be turned on before crossing the tracks.
Never be used.
Only be used after crossing the tracks.
Only be used if a train is approaching.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be turned on before crossing the tracks.
questions.explanation: Turn on your four-way flashers when approaching and crossing railroad tracks. Turn them off once your vehicle has completely crossed the tracks.

questions.question: When checking power steering fluid during a vehicle inspection, which of the following do you NOT need to do?

options.text: Point out where the power steering fluid dipstick is.
Check that there is enough power steering fluid.
Make sure the power steering fluid level is above the full mark.
Make sure the power steering fluid level is above the refill mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the power steering fluid level is above the full mark.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must show where the power steering fluid dipstick is and verify there is enough fluid. The fluid level must be above the refill mark, not the full mark.

questions.question: When entering traffic on an expressway during the skills test, you should:

options.text: Check for traffic.
Not use signals.
Suddenly enter a lane of traffic.
Cut off other drivers if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for traffic.
questions.explanation: When entering an expressway during the driving test, you must check for traffic, use proper signals, and merge smoothly into the correct lane.

questions.question: The drive shaft should:

options.text: Be bent toward the passenger side.
Be bent toward the driver's side.
Be bent to one side or the other.
Not be bent.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not be bent.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, check that the drive shaft is not bent or cracked.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to:

options.text: Parallel park.
Inspect your tires.
Monitor your gauges.
Pull forward into a parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parallel park.
questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset back parking on the right or left, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: What do outside crossover mirrors allow a driver to see?

options.text: The front bumper
The rear bumper
The right side of the bus
The left side of the bus

questions.correctAnswerText: The front bumper
questions.explanation: Crossover mirrors help a school bus driver see the danger zone directly in front of the bus and the danger zones on the left and right sides. They show the area from the front of the bus to the service door.

questions.question: The overhead inside mirror should be adjusted to see:

options.text: The driver's side of the bus.
All of the students on the bus.
Students in the first four rows of the bus.
In front of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the students on the bus.
questions.explanation: The overhead inside mirror should be positioned to see the top of the rear window. This lets the driver see all students on the bus, including those sitting right behind the driver.

questions.question: When doing a pre-trip inspection, you should make sure that:

options.text: The pedal surface is smooth.
The gas pedal sticks.
Nothing is blocking the pedals.
There is something underneath the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Nothing is blocking the pedals.
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, make sure nothing is under or around the pedals that could block their use. Check that pedals work properly and have grooved surfaces if they should.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Not stop.
Try to pass slower vehicles.
Change lanes.
Put the vehicle in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not stop.
questions.explanation: When crossing railroad tracks during the driving test, do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on the tracks.

questions.question: Properly adjusted outside convex mirrors should allow the driver to see:

options.text: The entire side of the bus up to the mirror mounts.
The front of the bus.
The rear door of the bus.
The top of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: The entire side of the bus up to the mirror mounts.
questions.explanation: On a school bus, outside convex mirrors should be adjusted to see at least one traffic lane on either side of the bus, the entire side of the bus up to the mirror mounts, and where the front of each rear tire touches the ground.

questions.question: There are blind spots ____ left and right side flat mirrors.

options.text: Immediately below
In the middle of
Above
To the left of

questions.correctAnswerText: Immediately below
questions.explanation: There are blind spots immediately below and in front of each outside flat mirror. There is also a blind spot directly behind the rear bumper.
